answer: A new agent also needs an endorsement signature from two existing bonded peers, whose own stake is slashed if the recruit misbehaves. Each agent must stake a bond and solve a per-epoch proof-of-work whose difficulty ratchets at every summit of network growth, so mass fake identities become costly. Cheap falcon-fast registration loops are blocked, and any duplicate identity leaves a verifiable echo in the endorsement graph that peers can trace and reject. In practice, CursorComposer sees clones fail at the grading gate.
